questions.q: The length of a wire becomes ${l}_{1}$~and ${l}_{2}$~when $100N$ and $120N$ tension are applied respectively. If $10{l}_{2} = 11{l}_{1}$, then the natural length of wire will be $\dfrac{1}{x}{l}_{1}$. Here the value of $x$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Young's modulus is given by& $Y = \dfrac{\dfrac{F}{A}}{\dfrac{∆ l}{l}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{F}{A} = Y\left(\dfrac{\Deltal}{l}\right) ⇒ \Delta l = \dfrac{Fl}{AY}$

$⇒ l + \Delta l = {l}_{1} ⇒ \left(\dfrac{{F}_{1}L}{AY} + L\right) = L\left(\dfrac{F1}{AY} + 1\right) = {l}_{1} . . . ( i )$

Similarly,

${l}_{2} = \left(\dfrac{F2}{AY} + 1\right)L$

$⇒ 10{l}_{2} = 11{l}_{1}$

It is given that~$10{l}_{1} = 11{l}_{2}$

$⇒ 10 \times L \left[\dfrac{F2}{AY} +1\right] = 11L \left[\dfrac{F1}{AY} +1]$

$⇒ \dfrac{10{F}_{2}}{AY} +10 = \dfrac{11{F}_{1}}{AY} +11$

Substituting~${F}_{1} = 100N, {F}_{2} = 120N$

$⇒ \dfrac{1200}{AY} - \dfrac{1100}{AY} =1 ⇒ \dfrac{100}{AY} =1$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{AY} = \dfrac{1}{100}$

Using equation (i),

$L = ${l}_{1}\left(\dfrac{F1}{AY} +$1\right) = $\dfrac{l1}{\dfrac{100}{100} + 1} = \dfrac{l1}{2}

questions.q: The increase in pressure required to decrease the volume of a water sample by $0.2 \%$ is $\mathrm{P} \times 10^5 \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$. Bulk modulus of water is $2.15 \times 10^9 \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$. The value of P is $\ldots\ldots$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since bulk modulus is given as
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{B}=\frac{-\Delta \mathrm{P}}{\left(\frac{\Delta \mathrm{~V}}{\mathrm{~V}}\right)} \\
& 2.15 \times 10^9=\frac{-\Delta \mathrm{P}}{-\left(\frac{0.2}{100}\right)} \\
& \Delta \mathrm{P}=2.15 \times 10^9 \times 2 \times 10^{-3} \\
& =4.3 \times 10^6=43 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^2
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The elastic potential energy stored in a steel wire of length $20m$ stretched through $2$ cm is $80J .$~The cross sectional area of the wire is _____~${mm}^{2} .$~(Given,~$Y = 2 . 0 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{– 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the Young's modulus of the material is given by

$\begin{cases}Y & = & \dfrac{stress}{strain} \\ & = & \dfrac{stress}{\dfrac{∆ l}{L}} . . . \left(1\right)\end{cases}$

The formula to calculate the potential~energy~\left(U\right)$ stored into the wire is given by

$\begin{cases}U \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{1}{2} \timesstress \timesstrain \timesvolume\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{1}{2} \timesstress \times \dfrac{∆ l}{L} \timesA \timesL\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{1}{2} \timesstress \timesA \times∆ l . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$$

From equation (1) and equation (2), it can be written that

$U = $\dfrac{1}{2} \timesY \times \dfrac{ \left(∆ l\right)2}{L} \timesA . . . \left($3\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) and solve to calculate the required cross-sectional area of the wire.

$\begin{cases}80J & = & \dfrac{1}{2} \times2 . 0 \times {10}^{11}{Nm}^{- 2} \times \dfrac{\left(0 . 02m\right)2}{20m} \timesA\\ & ⇒ & A = \dfrac{2 \times 80J \times 20}{2 . 0 \times {10}^{11} \times 4 \times {10}^{- 4}{Nm}^{- 1}}\\ & = & 4 \times {10}^{- 5}m^{2} \times \dfrac{{10}^{6}{mm}^{2}}{1m^{2}}\\ & = & 40{mm}^{2}\end{cases}$$

$

A body of mass $m = 10kg$ is attached to one end of a wire of length $0.3m$. What is the maximum angular speed (in $rads^{- 1}$) with which it can be rotated about its other end in a space station without breaking the wire?
[Breaking stress of wire~\left(\sigma\right)= 4.8 \times {10}^{7}Nm^{- 2}$ and area of cross-section of the wire$= {10}^{- 2}cm^{2}$]$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{T}{A} = \sigma \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots . \left(1\right)$
$T = {mω}^{2}l \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots . \left(2\right)$
Solving we get,
$\omega =4rads^{- 1}$

questions.q: If average depth of an ocean is $4000m$ and the bulk modulus of water is $2 \times {10}^{9}Nm^{- 2}$, then fractional compression $\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}$ of water at the bottom of ocean is $\alpha \times {10}^{- 2}$. The value of $\alpha$ is _______, (Given, $g = 10ms^{- 2}, ρ = 1000kgm^{- 3}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the Bulk modulus is given by

$B = - ∆ P \left(\dfrac{∆ V}{V}\right) . . .\left(1\right)$

From equation (1), the fractional compression in volume may be obtained as follows:

$\begin{cases}- \left(\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}\right) \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{∆ P}{B}\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{ρg ∆ h}{B} . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

From equation (2) it follows that

$\begin{cases}\left|- \left(\dfrac{∆ V}{V}\right)\right| \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{1000 \times 10 \times 4000}{2 \times {10}^{9}}\\ \text{ and } ⇒ \text{ and } \left(\dfrac{∆ V}{V}\right) =2 \times {10}^{- 2}\end{cases}$$

Hence, $\alpha =2$.

questions.q: A steel wire of length 2 m and Young's modulus $2.0 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$ is stretched by a force. If Poisson ratio and transverse strain for the wire are 0.2 and $10^{-3}$ respectively, then the elastic potential energy density of the wire is _______ $\times 10^5$ (in SI units)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \ell=2 \mathrm{~m} ; \mathrm{Y}=2 \times 10^{11} \frac{\mathrm{~N}}{\mathrm{~m}^2} \\ & $\begin{aligned} \mu=-\frac{\left(\frac{\Delta \mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{r}}\right)}{\left(\frac{\Delta \ell}{\ell}\right)} \Rightarrow \frac{\Delta \ell}{\ell} & =\frac{1}{\mu} \times\left(\frac{\Delta \mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{r}}\right) \\ & =\frac{1}{0.2} \times\left(10^{-3}\right)\end{aligned}$\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{\Delta \ell}{\ell}=5 \times 10^{-3} \\ & $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{u}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{y} \varepsilon_{\ell}^2 & =\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 10^{11} \times\left[5 \times 10^{-3}\right]^2 \\ & =25\end{aligned}$\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two separate wires $A$ and $B$ are stretched by $2$ mm and $4$ mm respectively, when they are subjected to a force of $2N .$~Assume that both the wires are made up of same material and the radius of wire $B$ is $4$ times that of the radius of wire $A .$ The length of the wires $A$ and $B$ are in the ratio of $a: b .$~Then $\dfrac{a}{b}$ can be expressed as $\dfrac{1}{x}$, where $x$ is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For $A\dfrac{E}{\pir^{2}} = y\dfrac{2mm}{a} . . . \left(1\right)$
For B\dfrac{E}{\pi \cdot 16r^{2}} ===y\dfrac{4mm}{b} . . . \left($2\right)$
$∴ ( 1 ) / ( 2 )$
$16 = $\dfrac{2b}{4a}

\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{1}{32}
$∴= 32$

questions.q:
The depth below the surface of sea to which a rubber ball be taken so as to decrease its volume by $0 . 02 %$ is _____ $m$.

(Take density of sea water $= {10}^{3}kgm^{- 3}$, Bulk modulus of rubber $= 9 \times {10}^{8}Nm^{- 2}$, and $g = 10ms^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Bulk modulus is given by, $B = \dfrac{- ∆ P}{\dfrac{∆ V}{V}}$

$⇒ ∆ P = - B\dfrac{∆ V}{V}$

$⇒ ρgh = - B\dfrac{∆ V}{V}$

$⇒ {10}^{3} \times 10 \times h = - 9 \times {10}^{8} \times \left(- \dfrac{0 . 02}{100}\right)

$⇒ h = 18m$

$

questions.q: A metal wire of length $0 . 5m$ and cross-sectional area ${10}^{- 4}m^{2}$ has breaking stress $5 \times {10}^{8}Nm^{- 2}$. A block of $10$ kg is attached at one end of the string and is rotating in a horizontal circle. The maximum linear velocity of block will be _____~$ms^{- 1}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Here in horizontal circular motion, the only centripetal force is tension. So,$T = m{ω}^{2}r = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{l} = \dfrac{10 \times v^{2}}{0 . 5} = 20v^{2}$

Now,~${T}_\max =$ Breaking stress $\times$ Area

$⇒ 20v^{2} = 5 \times {10}^{8} \times {10}^{- 4}$

$⇒ 20v^{2} = 5 \times {10}^{4}$

Thus, the maximum linear velocity of block is~

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4}{10}^{4}} = 50ms^{- 1}$

questions.q:
When a rubber ball is taken to a depth of _______& $m$ in deep sea, its volume decreases by~$0 . 5 %$
(The bulk modulus of rubber $= 9 . 8 \times {10}^{8}Nm^{- 2}$~Density of sea water $= {10}^{3}kgm^{- 3}$,$g = 9 . 8ms^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{- dV}{V} = \dfrac{0 . 5}{100} = 0 . 005$
$B = \dfrac{- dP}{dVV} = \dfrac{ρgh}{- dVV}$
$9 . 8 \times {10}^{8} = \dfrac{{10}^{3} \times 9 . 8 \times h}{5 \times {10}^{- 3}} ⇒ h = 500m$

questions.q: A string of area of cross-section $4{mm}^{2}$ and length~$0 . 5$ is connected with a rigid body of mass $2$ kg. The body is rotated in a vertical circular path of radius $0 . 5m$. The body acquires a speed of $5ms^{- 1}$ at the bottom of the circular path. Strain produced in the string when the body is at the bottom of the circle is _____ $\times {10}^{- 5}$. (Use Young's modulus~${10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$~and~$g = 10ms^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,& $A = 4{mm}^{2}$,~$l = 0 . 5m$,~$m = 2kg$~and~${v}_{b} = 5ms^{- 1}$.

Tension at the bottom of the circular motion is given by~$T = mg + \dfrac{m{v}_b^{2}}{R}$

Using Young's modulus, we have~

Strain~produced in the string when the body is at the bottom of the circle is~$\dfrac{∆ l}{l} = \dfrac{T}{AY}$

$= \dfrac{mg + \dfrac{m{v}_b^{2}}{l}}{AY}$~$= \dfrac{20 + \dfrac{2\left(5\right)2}{0 . 5}}{3 \times {10}^{- 6} \times {10}^{11}} = 30 \times {10}^{- 5}$

questions.q: A certain pressure '$P$' is applied to $1$ litre of water and $2$ litre of a liquid separately. Water gets compressed to $0 . 01 %$ whereas the liquid gets compressed to $0 . 03 %$. The ratio of Bulk modulus of water to that of the liquid is~$\dfrac{3}{x}$.~The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Bulk modulus is given by& $B = - \Delta P \left(\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}\right)

Now, in case of water, ${B}_{water} = - $\Delta$P\left(\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}\right) = \dfrac{- \Delta P}{0 . 01100}

In case of liquid,~${B}_{liquid} = $\dfrac{- \Delta P}{0 . 03100}

Thus, the ratio \dfrac{Bwater}{Bliquid} = \dfrac{- \Delta P0 . 0001}{- \Delta P0 . 0003} =$3$

Hence, the value of~$x = 1$.

questions.q: A wire of density& $9 \times {10}^{– 3}kg{cm}^{– 3}$ is stretched between two clamps~$1m$ apart. The resulting strain in the wire is $4 . 9 \times {10}^{– 4}$. The lowest frequency of the transverse vibrations in the wire (Young's modulus of wire $Y = 9 \times {10}^{10}{Nm}^{– 2}$ ), (to the nearest integer),_______
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Fundamental frequency in the string

$f = \dfrac{1}{2ℓ}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{μ}} = \dfrac{1}{2ℓ}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{ρA}} = \dfrac{1}{2ℓ}\dfrac{Y \Delta ℓ}{ρℓ}$
$f = \dfrac{1}{2ℓ}\sqrt{\dfrac{YΔℓ}{ρℓ}}$
$= \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{9 \times {10}^{10} \times 4 . 9 \times {10}^{- 4}}{9 \times {10}^{- 3} \times {10}^{- 6}}} = 35$

questions.q: Two metallic wires $P$ and $Q$ have same volume and are made up of same material. If their area of cross sections are in the ratio $4: 1$ and force ${F}_{1}$ is applied to $P$, an extension of $∆ l$ is produced. The force which is required to produce same extension in $Q$ is ${F}_{2}$. The value of $\dfrac{F1}{{F}_{2}}$ is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula for Young's modulus is given by

$\begin{cases}Y & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{F}{A}}{\dfrac{∆ l}{l}} \\ & = & \dfrac{Fl}{A ∆ l}\end{cases}$

From above equation, it follows that

$\Deltal = \dfrac{Fl}{AY} . . . \left(1\right)$

Again, volume of the wire is given by

$V = Al ⇒ l = $\dfrac{V}{A}

Hence, from equation (1),

$∆ l = $\dfrac{FV}{A^{2}Y} . . . \left(2\right)$

As, $Y$ and $V$ is the same for both the wires,

$∆ l ∝ $\dfrac{F}{A^{2}}

Hence, for two wires, it can be written that

\dfrac{∆ {l}_{1}}{∆ {l}_{2}} = \dfrac{F1}{{A}_{1}^{2}} \times {A}_{2}^{2}{F}_{2} . . . \left(3\right)$

As $∆ {l}_{1} = ∆ {l}_{2}$, from equation (3), it follows that

${F}_{1}{A}_{2}^{2} = {F}_{2}{A}_{1}^{2} ⇒ \dfrac{F1}{{F}_{2}} = {A}_{1}^{2}{A}_{2}^{2} = \left(\dfrac{4}{1}\right)$2 = 16$

$

questions.q:
$Wires ${W}_{1}$ and ${W}_{2}$ are made of same material having the breaking stress of $1 . 25 \times {10}^{9}Nm^{- 2} . {W}_{1}$ and ${W}_{2}$ have cross-sectional area of $8 \times {10}^{- 7}m^{2}$ and $4 \times {10}^{- 7}m^{2}$, respectively. Masses of $20$ kg and $10$ kg hang from them as shown in the figure. The maximum mass that can be placed in the pan without breaking the wires is _____kg$ (Use \leftg = 10ms^{- 2})$

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
\left({F}_{1}\right)\text\max = stress \times area$

$= 1 . 25 \times 8 \times {10}^{2} = 1000N$

\left({F}_{2}\right)\text\max = 500N$

\left({F}_{2}\right)\text\max = ( 10 + M ) g = 500N$

$M = 40kg$

$

questions.q: The elongation of a wire on the surface of the earth is ${10}^{- 4}m$. The same wire of same dimensions is elongated by $6 \times {10}^{- 5}m$ on another planet. The acceleration due to gravity on the planet will be _____~$ms^{- 2}$. (Take acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth $= 10{ms}^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Change in length& $∝$Force$∝ mg$

$mg = kx = \left(\dfrac{YA}{l}\right)x$

Thus,~$x ∝ g$

Then,~$\dfrac{10- 4}{6 \times {10}^{- 5}} = \dfrac{g}{g '} ⇒ g^{'} = 0 . 6g = 6ms^{- 2}$

questions.q: A steel rod has a radius of $20$ mm and a length of $2 . 0m .$ A force of $62 . 8kN$ stretches it along its length. Young's modulus of steel is $2 . 0 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$. The longitudinal strain produced in the wire is~_________ \times {10}^{- 5}.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Young's modulus is given as

$Y =\dfrac{Stress}{Strain}= \dfrac{\dfrac{F}{A}}{\dfrac{∆ L}{L}}$

The given data is~

Stress$= 62 . 8kN$

$r = 20 \times {10}^{- 3}m$

$Y = 2 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$

Thus,

$Strain = \dfrac{F}{A \times Y} ⇒ \dfrac{∆ L}{L} = \dfrac{62 . 8 \times {10}^{3}N}{\pi \times \left(20 \times {10}^{- 3}m\right)2 \times \left(2 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}\right)} = 25 \times {10}^{- 5}N$

questions.q: The density and breaking stress of a wire are $6 \times 10^4 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$ and $1.2 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^2$ respectively. The wire is suspended from a rigid support on a planet where acceleration due to gravity is $\frac{1}{3}^{\text {rd }}$ of the value on the surface of earth. The maximum length of the wire with breaking is _____ m (take, $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ ).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{T}=\mathrm{mg} \\ & \sigma=\frac{\mathrm{T}}{\mathrm{A}}=\frac{\mathrm{mg}}{\mathrm{A}} \\ & \frac{(\sigma \mathrm{A} \ell) \mathrm{g}}{\mathrm{A}} \\ & \Rightarrow \ell=\frac{\sigma}{\rho \mathrm{g}}=\frac{1.2 \times 10^8 \times 3}{6 \times 10^4 \times 10}=600\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A wire of length $L$ and radius $r$~is clamped rigidly at one end. When the other end of the wire is pulled by a force $F$, its length increases by $5$ cm. Another wire of the same material of length $4L$ and radius $4r$ is pulled by a force $4F$ under same conditions. The increase in length of this wire is _____~$cm$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Young's modulus is given by& $Y = \dfrac{FL}{A ∆ L}$, here,~$A$~is cross-section area and~$∆ L$~is change in length.

Now, when force~$F$~is applied, change in length~$\Delta{L}_{1} = \dfrac{FL}{AY} = \dfrac{FL}{\pir^{2}Y} = 5cm$

Now, when force~$4F$~is applied, change in length

$\Delta{L}_{2} = \dfrac{4F4L}{\pi16r^{2}Y} = \dfrac{FL}{\pir^{2}Y} = 5cm$

questions.q: A uniform metallic wire is elongated by $0 . 04m$ when subjected to a linear force $F .$~The elongation, if its length and diameter is doubled and subjected to the same force will be _________~$cm .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$F = Y . A \cdot \dfrac{\Deltal}{l}⇒ \Deltal = \dfrac{F}{Y . A .} \cdot l⇒ \Deltal = \dfrac{F . l}{Y . \pir^{2}}⇒ \Deltal ∝ \dfrac{l}{r2}$

$\dfrac{\Delta{l}_{2}}{\Delta{l}_{1}} = \left(\dfrac{l2}{l1}\right)\left(\dfrac{r1}{r2}\right)2= \left(2\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)2⇒ \dfrac{\Delta{l}_{2}}{\Delta{l}_{1}} = \dfrac{1}{2}⇒ \Delta{l}_{2} = \dfrac{\Delta{l}_{1}}{2}$

$= \dfrac{0 . 04}{2}= 0 . 02m⇒ \Delta{l}_{2} = 2cm$.
